locator: Table 1: non-AGC central volume and linear clearance; population-model methods/results
finding: Quartino and colleagues modeled serum trastuzumab exposure across clinical studies using two compartments and parallel linear and nonlinear elimination.
hypothesis_relevance: Provides the PK reference for asking how slower elimination changes exposure over time.
use_in_model: The reviewed volume and linear-clearance inputs provide the PK starting point. In the reference preset, tripling half-life reduces clearance at fixed volume, changing concentration and consequently occupancy.
limitation: Hypothesim reduces the published model to one linear compartment. Its curves are exploratory reductions, not reproduced patient predictions.

locator: Table 3: intact trastuzumab row; SPR methods 4.11
finding: Selis and colleagues compared intact trastuzumab with antibody fragments. Their SPR measurements report association and dissociation rates for intact trastuzumab against immobilized HER2.
hypothesis_relevance: Supplies the matched kinetic rates used to explore affinity changes alongside changes in elimination.
use_in_model: The intact-antibody rate pair provides the occupancy starting point, with KD calculated as koff/kon. In the reference preset, the affinity alternative lowers koff tenfold at fixed kon and does not change the PK concentration curve.
limitation: These are apparent assay kinetics transferred to an effective-site model, not measured tissue occupancy. Fragment engineering in this paper also motivates checking whether PK and affinity can really change independently.
